source.text: בֶּן־שְׁתֵּ֥ים עֶשְׂרֵ֛ה שָׁנָ֖ה מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה בְמָלְכ֑וֹ וַחֲמִשִּׁ֤ים וְחָמֵשׁ֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: A son of two [and] ten year[s was] Manasseh when he became king, and fifty and five year[s] he reigned in Jerusalem.

en.L: Manasseh [was] a son of twelve years when he became king, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem.
en.B: Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem.
en.R: Manasseh became king at the age of twelve, and he ruled in Jerusalem for fifty-five years.

decisions.choice: the opening of Manasseh's reign: parallel to 2 Kings 21:1, without the queen mother
decisions.reason: Verses 1-10 follow 2 Kings 21:1-10 closely. Here the words are the same as in Kings, except that Chronicles leaves out the name of Manasseh's mother, Hephzibah. From Manasseh on, Chronicles no longer names the mothers of the kings of Judah, though Kings goes on doing so.

decisions.choice: a son of twelve years: twelve years old
decisions.reason: Hebrew gives a person's age as being "a son of" so many years, as in 27:1.

decisions.choice: fifty-five years: the longest reign of any king of Judah
decisions.reason: Manasseh followed his father Hezekiah (32:33). His reign is the longest of any king of Judah or Israel. The years may include a time when he shared the throne with his father, since Hezekiah was given fifteen more years after his illness (2 Kings 20:6) and Manasseh was only twelve when he became king.

decisions.choice: Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-five years
decisions.reason: Worded as in 2 Kings 21:1 at each level, the accession formula kept throughout Kings and Chronicles.

source.text: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כְּתֽוֹעֲבוֹת֙ הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ הוֹרִ֣ישׁ יְהוָ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh, according to [the] abominations of the nations which dispossessed Yahweh from before [the] sons of Israel.

en.L: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, according to the abominations of the nations that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had driven out before the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.
en.B: He did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, following the detestable practices of the nations that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had driven out ahead of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.
en.R: He did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil. He copied the disgusting things that the nations had done before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} forced them out of the land for the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

decisions.choice: the same words as 2 Kings 21:2
decisions.reason: The verse is word for word the same as 2 Kings 21:2, and is worded the same way here.

decisions.choice: did what was evil in Yahweh's eyes: the bad verdict
decisions.reason: The verdict of the regnal formula. Manasseh's father Hezekiah had done what was right (29:2); the son undoes his father's work.

decisions.choice: abominations: practices Yahweh detests
decisions.reason: The word is used for what is utterly offensive to Yahweh, especially the worship and customs of the Canaanite nations. Deuteronomy 18:9-12 uses it of the very practices listed in verses 3-6.

decisions.choice: the nations Yahweh drove out: Judah takes up the sins for which the land was taken from them
decisions.reason: The nations lost the land because of these practices (Leviticus 18:24-28; Deuteronomy 9:4-5). If Judah does the same, it faces the same end.

decisions.choice: did the evil in [the] eyes of / did what was evil in the sight of / did what the LORD said was evil; abominations / detestable practices / disgusting things
decisions.reason: The verdict formula and the word for abominations, worded at each level as in 2 Kings 21:2.

source.text: וַיָּ֗שָׁב וַיִּ֨בֶן֙ אֶת־הַבָּמ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִתַּ֖ץ יְחִזְקִיָּ֣הוּ אָבִ֑יו וַיָּ֨קֶם מִזְבְּח֤וֹת לַבְּעָלִים֙ וַיַּ֣עַשׂ אֲשֵׁר֔וֹת וַיִּשְׁתַּ֨חוּ֙ לְכָל־צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֖ד אֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he returned and built the high places which had pulled down Hezekiah his father, and he set up altars for the Baals, and he made Asherahs, and he bowed down to all [the] host of the heavens and served them.

en.L: And he again built the high places that Hezekiah his father had pulled down, and he set up altars for the Baals and made Asherah poles, and he bowed down to all the host of the heavens and served them.
en.B: He rebuilt the high places that his father Hezekiah had pulled down. He set up altars for the Baals and made Asherah poles. He bowed down to all the host of heaven and served them.
en.R: He built again the hilltop shrines that his father Hezekiah had torn down. He set up altars to worship the Baals, and he made poles used to worship Asherah. He bowed down to the sun, moon and stars and worshiped them.

decisions.choice: differences from 2 Kings 21:3: "pulled down", the Baals and Asherahs in the plural, no mention of Ahab
decisions.reason: Kings says Hezekiah had "destroyed" the high places; Chronicles uses a verb for pulling down or breaking down, as in its account of Hezekiah's reform (31:1). Kings has "Baal" and "an Asherah"; Chronicles has the plurals, "the Baals" and "Asherahs", as it does for Ahaz (28:2) and for the reforms (34:4). Chronicles leaves out the comparison with "Ahab king of Israel".

decisions.choice: he returned and built: he rebuilt
decisions.reason: "Returned and built" is a Hebrew way of saying "built again". Manasseh undid his father's reform, in which Hezekiah had pulled down the high places and altars (31:1; 32:12).

decisions.choice: the Baals and Asherahs: the gods and goddess of Canaan
decisions.reason: Baal was the chief god of the Canaanites, worshiped in many local forms, and the plural "the Baals" covers them all. Asherah was a Canaanite goddess, and her symbol was a wooden pole or tree set up beside an altar.

decisions.choice: the host of the heavens: the sun, moon and stars worshiped as gods
decisions.reason: The "host" or army of the heavens is the sun, moon and stars (Deuteronomy 4:19). Israel was forbidden to bow down to them (Deuteronomy 17:3), as in 2 Kings 21:3.

decisions.choice: high places, Asherah poles, the host of heaven (Literal, Balanced); hilltop shrines, poles used to worship Asherah, the sun, moon and stars (Readable)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for these words in Samuel, Kings and Chronicles, as in 2 Kings 21:3. Literal says "pulled down" for the verb Chronicles uses, where 2 Kings 21:3 has "destroyed".

source.text: וּבָנָ֥ה מִזְבְּח֖וֹת בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁר֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֥ם יִֽהְיֶה־שְּׁמִ֖י לְעוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he built altars in [the] house of Yahweh, of which said Yahweh, In Jerusalem will be my name forever.

en.L: And he built altars in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, of which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said, "In Jerusalem my name will be forever."
en.B: He built altars in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the house about which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said, "My name will be in Jerusalem forever."
en.R: He even built altars inside the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. This was the place {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had spoken of when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "My name will be in Jerusalem forever."

decisions.choice: my name will be in Jerusalem forever: where 2 Kings 21:4 has "I will put my name"
decisions.reason: The verse follows 2 Kings 21:4, but Yahweh's words differ: Kings has "In Jerusalem I will put my name", Chronicles "In Jerusalem my name will be forever". Chronicles uses the same words in Yahweh's answer to Solomon (7:16). Yahweh had chosen Jerusalem as the place for his name (6:6; Deuteronomy 12:5, 11), and Manasseh sets up altars for other gods in the very house that bears it.

decisions.choice: altars: the altars for the host of heaven of verse 5
decisions.reason: Verse 5 says what these altars were for. Verse 4 first names the outrage, that they stood in Yahweh's own house.

decisions.choice: the house about which (Balanced); This was the place ... spoken of (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 21:4: Balanced repeats "the house" so that "about which" plainly refers to the temple, and Readable makes the clause a sentence of its own and adds "even" for the shock of the act. Readable says "temple" for Yahweh's "house".

source.text: וַיִּ֥בֶן מִזְבְּח֖וֹת לְכָל־צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם בִּשְׁתֵּ֖י חַצְר֥וֹת בֵּית־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he built altars to all [the] host of the heavens in [the] two courts of [the] house of Yahweh.

en.L: And he built altars to all the host of the heavens in the two courts of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: He built altars to all the host of heaven in the two courtyards of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: In both courtyards of the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, he built altars to worship the sun, moon and stars.

decisions.choice: the same words as 2 Kings 21:5
decisions.reason: The verse is the same as 2 Kings 21:5 and is worded as there.

decisions.choice: the two courts of the house of Yahweh: the inner and the outer court
decisions.reason: Solomon's temple had a court for the priests, where the altar of burnt offering stood, and a great outer court (4:9). Manasseh filled both with altars to the stars.

decisions.choice: the sun, moon and stars
decisions.reason: As in verse 3.

source.text: וְהוּא֩ הֶעֱבִ֨יר אֶת־בָּנָ֤יו בָּאֵשׁ֙ בְּגֵ֣י בֶן־הִנֹּ֔ם וְעוֹנֵ֤ן וְנִחֵשׁ֙ וְֽכִשֵּׁ֔ף וְעָ֥שָׂה א֖וֹב וְיִדְּעוֹנִ֑י הִרְבָּ֗ה לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הָרַ֛ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה לְהַכְעִיסֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he made pass his sons through the fire in [the] valley of Ben-hinnom, and he practiced soothsaying and interpreted omens and practiced sorcery, and he dealt with [a] medium and [a] spiritist; he increased to do the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh, to provoke him.

en.L: And he made his sons pass through the fire in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, and he practiced soothsaying and interpreted omens and practiced sorcery, and he dealt with a medium and a spiritist. He did much evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, provoking [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] to anger.
en.B: He made his sons pass through the fire in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, practiced fortune-telling, read omens and practiced sorcery, and consulted a medium and a spiritist. He did much evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, provoking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to anger.
en.R: He burned his own sons in the fire as sacrifices in the Valley of Ben-hinnom. He told fortunes, read signs to know the future and practiced witchcraft, and he asked mediums and spiritists to get messages from spirits. He did many things that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said were evil, and this made {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} angry.

decisions.choice: differences from 2 Kings 21:6: "his sons", the place named, sorcery added
decisions.reason: Kings says Manasseh made "his son" pass through the fire; Chronicles has "his sons" and names the place, the Valley of Ben-hinnom, as it does for Ahaz (28:3). Chronicles adds "practiced sorcery", one more of the practices Deuteronomy 18:10 forbids. It also has "a spiritist" where Kings has "spiritists".

decisions.choice: made his sons pass through the fire in the Valley of Ben-hinnom: offered his sons as burnt sacrifices
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 18:10 forbids this rite first in its list, and 12:31 shows that it meant burning children to a god. The Valley of Ben-hinnom lay south of Jerusalem; Topheth, the place of burning, was there (2 Kings 23:10; Jeremiah 7:31).

decisions.choice: soothsaying, omens, sorcery, a medium and a spiritist: the practices Deuteronomy 18:10-11 forbids
decisions.reason: The words are those of Deuteronomy 18:10-11. The first may be telling fortunes by reading the clouds; the second is reading omens (Genesis 44:5); the third is working spells or magic (Exodus 22:17). The medium and the spiritist are people who claimed to call up the spirits of the dead or to gain hidden knowledge from them (Leviticus 19:31; 1 Samuel 28:7).

decisions.choice: he did much evil, to provoke: the language of Deuteronomy's warnings
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 21:6. Deuteronomy 4:25 and 31:29 warn that Israel would do evil in Yahweh's eyes and provoke him to anger, and that exile would follow.

decisions.choice: soothsaying, interpreted omens, practiced sorcery (Literal); fortune-telling, read omens, practiced sorcery (Balanced); told fortunes, read signs to know the future, practiced witchcraft (Readable)
decisions.reason: The words used for these practices in Deuteronomy 18:10-11 and 2 Kings 21:6 at each level. Readable says "burned ... as sacrifices" for "made pass through the fire", as there, and keeps the plural "mediums and spiritists" of 2 Kings 21:6 because it speaks of the practice in general.

decisions.choice: him
decisions.reason: The verb "provoke to anger" has no object in Hebrew; the object is Yahweh. Literal brackets it.

source.text: וַיָּ֕שֶׂם אֶת־פֶּ֥סֶל הַסֶּ֖מֶל אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה בְּבֵ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָמַ֤ר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל־דָּוִיד֙ וְאֶל־שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בְנ֔וֹ בַּבַּ֨יִת הַזֶּ֜ה וּבִֽירוּשָׁלִַ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֤ר בָּחַ֨רְתִּי֙ מִכֹּל֙ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אָשִׂ֥ים אֶת־שְׁמִ֖י לְעֵילֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he set [the] image of the idol that he had made in [the] house of God, of which said God to David and to Solomon his son, In the house the this and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen from all [the] tribes of Israel, I will put my name forever;

en.L: And he set the carved image of the idol that he had made in the house of God, of which God had said to David and to Solomon his son, "In this house and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen from all the tribes of Israel, I will put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name forever.
en.B: He placed the carved idol he had made in the house of God, about which God had said to David and to his son Solomon, "In this house, and in Jerusalem, the city I chose from among all the tribes of Israel, I will put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name forever.
en.R: He made a carved idol and set it up in God's temple. This was the temple God had spoken about to David and his son Solomon. He had said, "I will put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name in this temple and in Jerusalem forever. I chose Jerusalem out of all the tribes of Israel.

decisions.choice: differences from 2 Kings 21:7: "the idol" for "the Asherah", and "God" for "Yahweh"
decisions.reason: Kings speaks of "the carved image of the Asherah"; Chronicles has "the carved image of the idol", without naming the goddess. Kings says "the house of which Yahweh had said"; Chronicles has "the house of God, of which God had said". The rest of the verse is the same.

decisions.choice: the carved image of the idol: a carved statue of a god
decisions.reason: The second word means a statue or figure. Deuteronomy 4:16 forbids making one, and Ezekiel 8:3, 5 sees an idol of this kind at the temple's north gate. Manasseh will remove it from the temple after he humbles himself (verse 15).

decisions.choice: in this house and in Jerusalem ... I will put my name forever: Yahweh's promise to David and Solomon
decisions.reason: The words recall what Yahweh said of the temple and of Jerusalem when Solomon dedicated it (6:5-6; 7:12, 16). The promise was given with a condition (7:17-22), and verse 8 recalls it. The idol stands where Yahweh's name was to stand forever.

decisions.choice: forever: the quotation runs on into verse 8
decisions.reason: The sentence goes on into verse 8, which adds the second half of Yahweh's word: the promise that Israel would stay in the land, and its condition.

decisions.choice: the carved image of the idol (Literal); the carved idol (Balanced); a carved idol (Readable)
decisions.reason: The two Hebrew nouns name one object, so Balanced and Readable join them. Readable splits Yahweh's words into two sentences and says "temple" for God's "house", as in 2 Kings 21:7.

source.text: וְלֹ֣א אוֹסִ֗יף לְהָסִיר֙ אֶת־רֶ֣גֶל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מֵעַל֙ הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶֽעֱמַ֖דְתִּי לַאֲבֹֽתֵיכֶ֑ם רַ֣ק׀אִם־יִשְׁמְר֣וּ לַעֲשׂ֗וֹת אֵ֚ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּיתִ֔ים לְכָל־הַתּוֹרָ֛ה וְהַֽחֻקִּ֥ים וְהַמִּשְׁפָּטִ֖ים בְּיַד־מֹשֶֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: and not I will add to remove [the] foot of Israel from upon the ground which I appointed for your fathers, only if they will keep to do all that I commanded them, as to all the law and the statutes and the judgments by [the] hand of Moses.

en.L: And I will not again remove the foot of Israel from the land that I appointed for your fathers, if only they are careful to do all that I have commanded them, all the law and the statutes and the judgments by the hand of Moses."
en.B: And I will not again make the feet of Israel leave the land I assigned to your ancestors, if only they will be careful to do all that I have commanded them, the whole law, the statutes and the rulings given through Moses."
en.R: I will not make the people of Israel leave the land I set aside for your ancestors again. But they must be careful to obey everything I have commanded them. They must obey the whole law, all the laws and rules I gave them through Moses."

decisions.choice: differences from 2 Kings 21:8
decisions.reason: Kings says "make the foot of Israel wander"; Chronicles says "remove the foot of Israel". Kings has "the land that I gave to their fathers"; Chronicles has "that I appointed for your fathers". Kings ends "all the law that my servant Moses commanded them"; Chronicles has "all the law and the statutes and the judgments by the hand of Moses". The promise and its condition are the same.

decisions.choice: remove the foot of Israel: drive Israel from its land
decisions.reason: To remove someone's foot from the land is to put them out of it. The promise was that Israel would be settled for good (2 Samuel 7:10; 1 Chronicles 17:9).

decisions.choice: your fathers: Yahweh turns to address the people
decisions.reason: The quotation is addressed to David and Solomon (verse 7), but here "your fathers" speaks to Israel, and the next clause goes back to "they". The change of person reflects a promise meant for the whole people. The Hebrew wording is kept.

decisions.choice: only if they are careful to do: the condition of the promise
decisions.reason: The promise of the land was never without condition (7:19-20; Deuteronomy 28:63-64). The words prepare for verse 10: they paid no attention.

decisions.choice: the law, the statutes and the judgments by the hand of Moses: all Yahweh's instruction given through Moses
decisions.reason: "Law" (torah) means the whole of Yahweh's instruction; "statutes" and "judgments" name its laws and rulings, as in Deuteronomy 4:1, 8. "By the hand of" means through Moses as the go-between.

decisions.choice: make the feet of Israel leave (Balanced); make the people of Israel leave (Readable); assigned / set aside
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of the feet but says "make ... leave", since "remove the feet" is not natural English; it says "feet", as English uses the plural for a people, and "ancestors" for "fathers". Readable says "the people of Israel". "Assigned" and "set aside" render "appointed", which differs from "gave" in 2 Kings 21:8.

decisions.choice: statutes, judgments (Literal); statutes, rulings (Balanced); laws, rules (Readable)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for these words in the books from Exodus on.

source.text: וַיֶּ֣תַע מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה אֶת־יְהוּדָ֖ה וְיֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת רָ֔ע מִן־הַ֨גּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ הִשְׁמִ֣יד יְהוָ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And led astray Manasseh Judah and [the] inhabitants of Jerusalem to do evil more than the nations which destroyed Yahweh from before [the] sons of Israel.

en.L: And Manasseh led Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem astray to do evil more than the nations that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had destroyed before the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.
en.B: Manasseh led Judah and the people of Jerusalem astray, so that they did more evil than the nations {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had destroyed ahead of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.
en.R: Manasseh led the people of Judah and Jerusalem to do wrong. They did even more evil things than the nations {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had wiped out to make room for the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

decisions.choice: differences from 2 Kings 21:9: "Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem" named; "they did not listen" moved to verse 10
decisions.reason: Kings begins "But they did not listen, and Manasseh led them astray". Chronicles names those he led astray, "Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem", a pair it often uses for the people of the kingdom (20:18; 32:33). The people's refusal to listen comes in verse 10, after Yahweh has spoken.

decisions.choice: led astray: made them wander from the right way
decisions.reason: The verb means to cause someone to go astray, like a lost animal. It is the opposite of keeping to the way Yahweh commanded (verse 8).

decisions.choice: more evil than the nations Yahweh destroyed
decisions.reason: The nations of Canaan were destroyed for their practices (verse 2). Judah now goes beyond them, so it has even less claim to the land than they had.

decisions.choice: the people of Jerusalem; to make room for (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "people" for "inhabitants". Readable spells out what "destroyed before" Israel meant, as in 2 Kings 21:9.

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־מְנַשֶּׁ֥ה וְאֶל־עַמּ֖וֹ וְלֹ֥א הִקְשִֽׁיבוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Manasseh and to his people, and not they paid attention.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Manasseh and to his people, but they did not pay attention.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Manasseh and his people, but they paid no attention.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Manasseh and his people, but they would not listen.

decisions.choice: a short summary in place of the prophets' oracle of 2 Kings 21:10-15
decisions.reason: Kings tells how Yahweh spoke "by the hand of his servants the prophets" and gives their long word of judgment on Jerusalem and Judah (2 Kings 21:10-15), and adds Manasseh's shedding of innocent blood (21:16). Chronicles says only that Yahweh spoke to Manasseh and his people and that they paid no attention, and turns at once to what happened to Manasseh himself. Verse 18 says that the words came through seers who spoke in Yahweh's name.

decisions.choice: paid attention: listened closely, took heed
decisions.reason: The verb means to turn the ear and listen with care. The same verb is used of warnings that went unheeded before the exile (Jeremiah 6:10, 17; Zechariah 7:11). It takes up the "they did not listen" of 2 Kings 21:9.

decisions.choice: would not listen
decisions.reason: Readable says the people refused to listen, which is what "did not pay attention" means here.

source.text: וַיָּבֵ֨א יְהוָ֜ה עֲלֵיהֶ֗ם אֶת־שָׂרֵ֤י הַצָּבָא֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר וַיִּלְכְּד֥וּ אֶת־מְנַשֶּׁ֖ה בַּחֹחִ֑ים וַיַּֽאַסְרֻ֨הוּ֙ בַּֽנְחֻשְׁתַּ֔יִם וַיּוֹלִיכֻ֖הוּ בָּבֶֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And brought Yahweh upon them the commanders of the army which [belonged] to [the] king of Assyria, and they captured Manasseh with the hooks, and they bound him with the bronze fetters, and they brought him to Babylon.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} brought upon them the commanders of the army of the king of Assyria, and they captured Manasseh with hooks and bound him with bronze fetters and brought him to Babylon.
en.B: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} brought against them the commanders of the army of the king of Assyria, who captured Manasseh with hooks, bound him with bronze chains and took him to Babylon.
en.R: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent the army commanders of the king of Assyria against them. They captured Manasseh and led him away with hooks. They bound him with bronze chains and took him to Babylon.

decisions.choice: the king of Assyria and Babylon: Manasseh was Assyria's subject king
decisions.reason: Verses 11-17 have no parallel in Kings. In Manasseh's day Assyria ruled the whole region, and Babylon was under the Assyrian king. Assyrian records of the period name "Manasseh king of Judah" among the kings who paid tribute and supplied materials for the Assyrian king's building work. The text does not say which king of Assyria this was or when it happened.

decisions.choice: with hooks: led away like a captured animal
alternatives: among the thorns (where he was hiding)
decisions.reason: The word means thorns or hooks (Job 40:26, of a hook put through a beast's jaw). Assyrian pictures show captives led by a hook or ring through the nose or lip, and Ezekiel 19:4, 9 pictures kings of Judah led away with hooks to Egypt and to Babylon. The words could also mean that he was caught "among the thorns", where he had hidden (1 Samuel 13:6).

decisions.choice: bronze fetters: a pair of bronze chains
decisions.reason: The word is dual, a pair of shackles for the hands or feet. Samson (Judges 16:21) and Zedekiah (2 Kings 25:7) were bound the same way as prisoners.

decisions.choice: Yahweh brought upon them: the capture is Yahweh's doing
decisions.reason: The people would not listen to Yahweh's word (verse 10), so he brings the Assyrian commanders upon them. Chronicles often tells how a king who forsakes Yahweh is handed over to his enemies (12:5; 24:24; 28:5).

decisions.choice: the commanders of the army (Literal, Balanced); the army commanders (Readable)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for the commander of the army in these books, here in the plural. Literal leaves out the "which [belonged] to" of the Hebrew, which only shows whose army it was.

decisions.choice: led him away with hooks
decisions.reason: Readable says what the hooks were for, following the reading chosen in m2.

source.text: וּכְהָצֵ֣ר ל֔וֹ חִלָּ֕ה אֶת־פְּנֵ֖י יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑יו וַיִּכָּנַ֣ע מְאֹ֔ד מִלִּפְנֵ֖י אֱלֹהֵ֥י אֲבֹתָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And when distressing to him, he entreated [the] face of Yahweh his God, and he humbled himself greatly before [the] God of his fathers.

en.L: And when he was in distress, he implored the face of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God, and he humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers.
en.B: In his distress he sought the favor of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God and humbled himself deeply before the God of his ancestors.
en.R: When Manasseh was in trouble, he begged {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God to be kind to him. He made himself very humble before the God of his ancestors.

decisions.choice: implored the face of Yahweh: sought his favor
decisions.reason: The phrase means to soften someone's face, that is, to seek the favor of someone who is angry, as in Exodus 32:11 and 1 Kings 13:6.

decisions.choice: humbled himself: the turning Yahweh promised to hear
decisions.reason: Yahweh had promised Solomon, "if my people ... humble themselves and pray and seek my face ... I will hear from heaven" (7:14). Manasseh does each part of it: he seeks Yahweh's face, humbles himself and prays (verse 13). Chronicles uses this verb for kings who turn back to Yahweh (12:6-7, 12; 32:26).

decisions.choice: his God, the God of his fathers
decisions.reason: Manasseh had served other gods (verses 3-7), yet in his distress he turns to Yahweh as "his God" and as the God of his ancestors, David and Hezekiah. The words mark his return to the faith he had abandoned.

decisions.choice: implored (Literal); sought the favor of (Balanced); begged ... to be kind (Readable)
decisions.reason: Worded as in Exodus 32:11. Literal says "when he was in distress" for the Hebrew "when it distressed him".

source.text: וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֣ל אֵלָ֗יו וַיֵּעָ֤תֶר לוֹ֙ וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע תְּחִנָּת֔וֹ וַיְשִׁיבֵ֥הוּ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם לְמַלְכוּת֑וֹ וַיֵּ֣דַע מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה ה֥וּא הָֽאֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And he prayed to him, and he was entreated by him and heard his supplication and brought him back [to] Jerusalem to his kingdom; and knew Manasseh that Yahweh, he [is] the God.

en.L: And he prayed to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was entreated by him and heard his supplication and brought him back to Jerusalem, to his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [is] God.
en.B: He prayed to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was moved by his prayer. He heard his plea for mercy and brought him back to Jerusalem, to his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is God.
en.R: He prayed to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} listened to him. God heard his cry for mercy and brought him back to Jerusalem to rule his kingdom again. Then Manasseh knew that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is the true God.

decisions.choice: he was entreated by him: God let himself be moved by his prayer
decisions.reason: This form of the verb means to let oneself be moved by a plea and to grant it (1 Chronicles 5:20; 2 Samuel 24:25). The subject is God, to whom Manasseh prayed.

decisions.choice: supplication: a plea for mercy
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "to be gracious" and names a prayer asking for grace, as in Solomon's prayer (6:19, 29, 35, 39).

decisions.choice: brought him back to Jerusalem, to his kingdom: the answer to a humbled king
decisions.reason: Solomon had prayed that if Israel were taken captive to a foreign land and turned to Yahweh there with all their heart, he would hear and forgive (6:36-39). Manasseh's story shows that prayer answered in one man: a captive king, taken away for his sin, is brought home when he humbles himself.

decisions.choice: Manasseh knew that Yahweh, he is God: the confession of Israel
decisions.reason: The words are those of Deuteronomy 4:35, 39 and of the people on Mount Carmel (1 Kings 18:39). Manasseh, who had served many gods, now knows by what happened to him that Yahweh alone is God.

decisions.choice: the LORD is God (Balanced); the LORD is the true God (Readable)
decisions.reason: The pronoun "he" repeats the subject for emphasis. Literal keeps it, as in 1 Kings 18:39; Balanced leaves it out, and Readable carries the emphasis with "the true God", as there. Balanced and Readable begin a new sentence after the prayer, and Readable says "God" to make clear who heard.

decisions.choice: to rule his kingdom again
decisions.reason: Readable says what "to his kingdom" means: he was king again.

source.text: וְאַחֲרֵי־כֵ֡ן בָּנָ֣ה חוֹמָ֣ה חִֽיצוֹנָ֣ה׀לְעִיר־דָּוִ֡יד מַעְרָבָה֩ לְגִיח֨וֹן בַּנַּ֜חַל וְלָב֨וֹא בְשַׁ֤עַר הַדָּגִים֙ וְסָבַ֣ב לָעֹ֔פֶל וַיַּגְבִּיהֶ֖הָ מְאֹ֑ד וַיָּ֧שֶׂם שָֽׂרֵי־חַ֛יִל בְּכָל־הֶעָרִ֥ים הַבְּצֻר֖וֹת בִּיהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And after thus he built [an] outer wall to [the] city of David, westward to Gihon in the valley, and to [the] entering at [the] gate of the fish, and he went around to the Ophel and made it high very; and he put commanders of [the] force in all the cities the fortified in Judah.

en.L: And after this he built an outer wall for the City of David, west of Gihon in the valley, and as far as the entrance at the Fish Gate, and it went around the Ophel, and he made it very high. And he put commanders of the army in all the fortified cities in Judah.
en.B: After this he built an outer wall for the City of David, west of Gihon in the valley, as far as the entrance at the Fish Gate. He carried it around the Ophel and made it very high. He also stationed army commanders in all the fortified cities of Judah.
en.R: After this, Manasseh built an outer wall for the City of David. It ran west of the Gihon spring in the Kidron Valley as far as the Fish Gate, and went around the hill called Ophel. He made the wall very high. He also put army commanders in all the fortified cities of Judah.

decisions.choice: an outer wall, west of Gihon in the valley: a new wall on the east side of the City of David
decisions.reason: Gihon was the spring on the east side of the City of David, in the Kidron Valley (32:30; 1 Kings 1:33). A wall "west of Gihon" ran along the slope above the spring, outside the older wall. Hezekiah had also built an outer wall (32:5).

decisions.choice: the Fish Gate and the Ophel
decisions.reason: The Fish Gate was on the north side of the city (Nehemiah 3:3; Zephaniah 1:10), perhaps named for the fish brought in to sell. The Ophel was the raised ground between the City of David and the temple, which Jotham had also built on (27:3).

decisions.choice: and it went around the Ophel, and he made it very high
decisions.reason: The first verb may describe the course of the wall ("it went around") or Manasseh's work ("he carried it around"). The sense is the same: the wall enclosed the Ophel.

decisions.choice: after this: building and strength follow his return to Yahweh
decisions.reason: In Chronicles, building cities and walls and stationing troops are signs of Yahweh's blessing on a faithful king (11:5-12; 14:5-6; 26:9; 32:5). Manasseh's building comes "after this", after he humbled himself and was restored.

decisions.choice: commanders of the army (Literal); army commanders (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Sar in a military setting is "commander" at every level. The word with it here means force or army.

decisions.choice: the Gihon spring in the Kidron Valley; the hill called Ophel
decisions.reason: Readable names the spring and the valley and says what the Ophel was (m1, m2).

source.text: וַ֠יָּסַר אֶת־אֱלֹהֵ֨י הַנֵּכָ֤ר וְאֶת־הַסֶּ֨מֶל֙ מִבֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה וְכָל־הַֽמִּזְבְּח֗וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּנָ֛ה בְּהַ֥ר בֵּית־יְהוָ֖ה וּבִירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַיַּשְׁלֵ֖ךְ ח֥וּצָה לָעִֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he removed [the] gods of the foreignness and the idol from [the] house of Yahweh, and all the altars which he had built on [the] mountain of [the] house of Yahweh and in Jerusalem, and he threw [them] outside to the city.

en.L: And he removed the foreign gods and the idol from the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and all the altars that he had built on the mountain of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and in Jerusalem, and he threw [them] outside the city.
en.B: He removed the foreign gods from the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and the idol as well, together with every altar he had built on the temple mount and elsewhere in Jerusalem, and threw them outside the city.
en.R: He took the foreign gods out of the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and the idol too. He also took away all the altars he had built on the hill where the temple stood and in Jerusalem, and he threw them out of the city.

decisions.choice: the idol and the altars: undoing what he had done in verses 4-7
decisions.reason: The idol is the one he had set in the house of God (verse 7), and the altars are those of verses 4-5. Kings does not tell of this reform. 2 Kings 23:12 says that Josiah later tore down the altars Manasseh had made in the two courts; Chronicles says only that Manasseh removed them and threw them out, so they may have been set up again under Amon (verse 22).

decisions.choice: the gods of the foreign: gods belonging to other peoples
decisions.reason: The phrase means gods that are foreign to Israel, as in Genesis 35:2, Joshua 24:20 and 1 Samuel 7:3. It sums up the Baals, the Asherahs and the host of heaven (verse 3).

decisions.choice: the mountain of the house of Yahweh: the hill on which the temple stood
decisions.reason: The temple stood on the hill north of the City of David (3:1). The altars there were the ones in the temple courts (verse 5).

decisions.choice: the temple mount (Balanced); the hill where the temple stood (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what "the mountain of the house of the LORD" means (m3). Balanced adds "elsewhere" because the temple mount was itself in Jerusalem. Literal supplies "them" after "threw".

source.text: וַיִּ֨בֶן֙ אֶת־מִזְבַּ֣ח יְהוָ֔ה וַיִּזְבַּ֣ח עָלָ֔יו זִבְחֵ֥י שְׁלָמִ֖ים וְתוֹדָ֑ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לִֽיהוּדָ֔ה לַעֲב֕וֹד אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And he built the altar of Yahweh and sacrificed on it sacrifices of peace offerings and thanksgiving, and he said to Judah to serve Yahweh [the] God of Israel.

en.L: And he rebuilt the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and sacrificed on it sacrifices of peace offerings and thanksgiving, and he told Judah to serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.
en.B: He restored the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and offered on it peace offerings and thank offerings, and he commanded Judah to serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.
en.R: He repaired the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and offered peace offerings and offerings to give thanks on it. He told the people of Judah to worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.

decisions.choice: built: the reading given in the margin (qere)
alternatives: he set in order the altar
decisions.reason: The letters written in the Hebrew text (ketiv) read "he set up" or "he set in order"; the reading passed down for reading aloud (qere) is "he built", as in the data followed here. Either way the sense is that Manasseh restored Yahweh's altar to its use.

decisions.choice: built the altar: rebuilt or restored it
decisions.reason: The altar of Yahweh already stood in the temple court (4:1; 29:18). To "build" it here is to repair it and make it fit for use again, after the years when other altars filled the courts (verses 4-5).

decisions.choice: peace offerings and thank offerings: sacrifices shared in a meal
decisions.reason: Peace offerings were eaten in part by the worshipers (Leviticus 3; 7:11-15), and the thank offering was a kind of peace offering given in thanks for help received (Leviticus 7:12). Manasseh thanks Yahweh for bringing him home.

decisions.choice: said to Judah to serve: commanded them to worship
decisions.reason: "Said" here has the force of a king's command, as in 14:3 and 29:21. To serve Yahweh is to worship him alone.

decisions.choice: rebuilt (Literal); restored (Balanced); repaired (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb is "build", but the altar already stood (m2), so each level says it was built again. Readable says "worship" for "serve" and "offerings to give thanks" for "thanksgiving".

source.text: אֲבָל֙ ע֣וֹד הָעָ֔ם זֹבְחִ֖ים בַּבָּמ֑וֹת רַ֖ק לַיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: But still the people [were] sacrificing at the high places, only to Yahweh their God.

en.L: But still the people [were] sacrificing at the high places, only to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God.
en.B: Even so, the people still sacrificed at the high places, though only to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God.
en.R: But the people still offered sacrifices at the hilltop shrines, though they offered them only to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God.

decisions.choice: at the high places, only to Yahweh: right worship in the wrong place
decisions.reason: The people no longer sacrificed to other gods, but they still did so at local shrines, not at the one place Yahweh had chosen (Deuteronomy 12:13-14). Kings often says the same of kings who were otherwise faithful (1 Kings 15:14; 2 Kings 12:4; 15:4). Hezekiah had removed the high places (31:1), and Manasseh had rebuilt them (verse 3).

decisions.choice: but: a limit on the reform
decisions.reason: The word marks a contrast with what has just been said, as in 19:3: Manasseh's reform did not reach everything.

decisions.choice: hilltop shrines
decisions.reason: The settled Readable wording for the high places.

source.text: וְיֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֣י מְנַשֶּׁה֮ וּתְפִלָּת֣וֹ אֶל־אֱלֹהָיו֒ וְדִבְרֵי֙ הַֽחֹזִ֔ים הַֽמְדַבְּרִ֣ים אֵלָ֔יו בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל הִנָּ֕ם עַל־דִּבְרֵ֖י מַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] rest of [the] matters of Manasseh, and his prayer to his God, and [the] words of the seers who spoke to him in [the] name of Yahweh [the] God of Israel, look, they [are] on [the] matters of [the] kings of Israel.

en.L: And the rest of the matters of Manasseh, and his prayer to his God, and the words of the seers who spoke to him in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, look, they [are] in the matters of the kings of Israel.
en.B: The rest of the acts of Manasseh, including the prayer he made to his God and what the seers said to him in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, are found in the Records of the Kings of Israel.
en.R: Everything else Manasseh did, his prayer to his God, and the messages the seers gave him in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, are all in the records of the kings of Israel. (Seers were prophets who received messages from God.)

decisions.choice: the sources formula, in Chronicles' form; parallel to 2 Kings 21:17
decisions.reason: Kings speaks of "the rest of the matters of Manasseh and all that he did, and his sin", written in the record of the kings of Judah. Chronicles names instead his prayer and the words of the seers, and the record of "the kings of Israel". Chronicles calls the kings of Judah kings of Israel, since they were David's line and ruled what was left of Israel (20:34).

decisions.choice: his prayer to his God: the prayer of verses 12-13, not kept in the Bible
decisions.reason: The prayer itself is not given. A short prayer under Manasseh's name is found in some ancient Greek and Latin Bibles; it was written much later and is not part of the Hebrew Bible.

decisions.choice: the seers who spoke to him in the name of Yahweh: the prophets of verse 10
decisions.reason: "Seer" is an older title for a prophet, one to whom God shows things (1 Samuel 9:9). These are the messengers through whom Yahweh spoke to Manasseh (verse 10; 2 Kings 21:10). The same Hebrew word stands for Manasseh's "matters", the seers' "words" and the "matters" of the kings, that is, their recorded history.

decisions.choice: look, they are: pointing the reader to the record
decisions.reason: The pointing word draws attention to where the record can be found, as in 27:7.

decisions.choice: the matters (Literal); the acts, the Records of the Kings of Israel (Balanced); the records of the kings of Israel (Readable)
decisions.reason: As for the sources formula elsewhere in Chronicles, Balanced says "the acts" for Manasseh's "matters" and writes the source as a title, and Readable keeps it plain. "Look" is carried by the plain statement.

decisions.choice: (Seers were prophets who received messages from God.)
decisions.reason: Readable explains "seer" once in this chapter, as at 19:2.

source.text: וּתְפִלָּת֣וֹ וְהֵֽעָתֶר־לוֹ֮ וְכָל־חַטָּאת֣וֹ וּמַעְלוֹ֒ וְהַמְּקֹמ֗וֹת אֲשֶׁר֩ בָּנָ֨ה בָהֶ֤ם בָּמוֹת֙ וְהֶעֱמִיד֙ הָאֲשֵׁרִ֣ים וְהַפְּסִלִ֔ים לִפְנֵ֖י הִכָּנְע֑וֹ הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֔ים עַ֖ל דִּבְרֵ֥י חוֹזָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And his prayer and being entreated by him, and all his sin and his unfaithfulness, and the places where he built in them high places and set up the Asherahs and the carved images before he humbled himself, look, they [are] written on [the] words of Hozai.

en.L: And his prayer, and how [God] was entreated by him, and all his sin and his unfaithfulness, and the places where he built high places and set up the Asherah poles and the carved images before he humbled himself, look, they [are] written in the words of Hozai.
en.B: His prayer and how God answered his plea, every sin and act of unfaithfulness, and the places where he built high places and erected Asherah poles and carved idols before he humbled himself, are written in the records of Hozai.
en.R: His prayer and how God answered it are written in the records of Hozai. So are all his sins and the ways he was unfaithful to God. They tell where he built hilltop shrines and set up poles used to worship Asherah and carved idols before he humbled himself.

decisions.choice: Hozai: the name in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text reads "Hozai", a name found nowhere else. The ancient Greek translation reads "the seers", as in verse 18, and a slight change to the Hebrew letters would give that reading or "his seers". The Hebrew text is followed; if the other reading is right, the source is the same writings of the seers named in verse 18.

decisions.choice: being entreated by him: how God let himself be moved by Manasseh's prayer
decisions.reason: The verb of verse 13 is here a noun-like form with no stated subject; the one who was entreated is God.

decisions.choice: unfaithfulness: breaking faith with Yahweh
decisions.reason: The word means acting treacherously against one to whom loyalty is owed. Chronicles uses it for the sin that brought Saul down and later the exile (1 Chronicles 10:13; 2 Chronicles 28:19; 36:14).

decisions.choice: high places, Asherah poles, carved images before he humbled himself
decisions.reason: These are the works of verses 3-7. Chronicles records the sins as well as the prayer, and dates them to the time "before he humbled himself".

decisions.choice: how God answered his plea; carved idols; the Records of Hozai (Balanced); the records of Hozai (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God as the one entreated (m2). As in verse 18, Balanced writes the source as a title. Readable splits the long list into sentences and puts the source first.

decisions.choice: Asherah poles, high places (Literal, Balanced); poles used to worship Asherah, hilltop shrines (Readable)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for these words, as in verse 3.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב מְנַשֶּׁה֙ עִם־אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻ֖הוּ בֵּית֑וֹ וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אָמ֥וֹן בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And lay down Manasseh with his fathers, and they buried him [in] his house; and reigned Amon his son in his place.

en.L: And Manasseh lay down with his fathers, and they buried him [at] his house, and Amon his son reigned in his place.
en.B: Then Manasseh rested with his ancestors, and they buried him at his palace. His son Amon became king in his place.
en.R: Then Manasseh died and was buried at his palace. His son Amon became king after him.

decisions.choice: buried at his house: 2 Kings 21:18 says "in the garden of his house, in the garden of Uzza"
decisions.reason: Chronicles says only "his house". Kings says Manasseh was buried in the garden of his palace, the garden of Uzza, not in the royal tombs in the City of David. The ancient Greek translation of Chronicles reads "in the garden of his house", as in Kings.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers: died
decisions.reason: The death formula, as in 2 Kings 21:18.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers / rested with his ancestors / died
decisions.reason: The death formula as worded at each level. Balanced and Readable say "palace" for the king's "house"; Literal brackets "at", which the Hebrew leaves unsaid.

source.text: בֶּן־עֶשְׂרִ֧ים וּשְׁתַּ֛יִם שָׁנָ֖ה אָמ֣וֹן בְּמָלְכ֑וֹ וּשְׁתַּ֣יִם שָׁנִ֔ים מָלַ֖ךְ בִּֽירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: A son of twenty and two year[s was] Amon when he became king, and two years he reigned in Jerusalem.

en.L: Amon [was] a son of twenty-two years when he became king, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem.
en.B: Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem.
en.R: Amon became king at the age of twenty-two, and he ruled in Jerusalem for two years.

decisions.choice: parallel to 2 Kings 21:19, without the queen mother
decisions.reason: The words are those of 2 Kings 21:19, which goes on to name Amon's mother, Meshullemeth daughter of Haruz from Jotbah. Chronicles leaves her out, as in verse 1.

decisions.choice: a son of twenty-two years: twenty-two years old
decisions.reason: As in verse 1.

decisions.choice: Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned two years
decisions.reason: Worded as in 2 Kings 21:19 at each level.

source.text: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ הָרַע֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה אָבִ֑יו וּֽלְכָל־הַפְּסִילִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשָׂה֙ מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה אָבִ֔יו זִבַּ֥ח אָמ֖וֹן וַיַּֽעַבְדֵֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh, as had done Manasseh his father; and to all the carved images which had made Manasseh his father sacrificed Amon, and he served them.

en.L: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, as Manasseh his father had done; and Amon sacrificed to all the carved images that Manasseh his father had made, and he served them.
en.B: He did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, as his father Manasseh had done, offering sacrifices to all the carved idols his father had made and serving them.
en.R: He did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil, just as his father Manasseh had done. He offered sacrifices to all the carved idols his father Manasseh had made, and he worshiped them.

decisions.choice: parallel to 2 Kings 21:20-21, more briefly and with sacrifice to the carved images
decisions.reason: The verdict is the same as in 2 Kings 21:20. Kings goes on to say that Amon walked in all his father's way, served the idols his father had served and bowed down to them, and forsook Yahweh (21:21-22). Chronicles says instead that he sacrificed to the carved images his father had made and served them.

decisions.choice: the carved images that Manasseh had made: the son takes up what the father had left
decisions.reason: These are the images Manasseh set up before he humbled himself (verse 19). Amon follows his father's early sin, not his repentance (verse 23). Verse 15 tells only of the foreign gods and the idol being removed from the temple; the text does not say where these images were.

decisions.choice: did the evil in [the] eyes of / did what was evil in the sight of / did what the LORD said was evil
decisions.reason: The verdict formula, worded as in 2 Kings 21:20. Readable says "worshiped" for "served".

source.text: וְלֹ֤א נִכְנַע֙ מִלִּפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה כְּהִכָּנַ֖ע מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה אָבִ֑יו כִּ֛י ה֥וּא אָמ֖וֹן הִרְבָּ֥ה אַשְׁמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And not he humbled himself before Yahweh as humbled himself Manasseh his father, for he, Amon, increased guilt.

en.L: And he did not humble himself before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as Manasseh his father had humbled himself, but he, Amon, increased guilt.
en.B: Unlike his father Manasseh, he did not humble himself before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Instead Amon added more and more to his guilt.
en.R: But he did not humble himself before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the way his father Manasseh had. Instead, Amon kept adding to his guilt.

decisions.choice: he did not humble himself as Manasseh had: the son is measured by his father's repentance
decisions.reason: This verse has no parallel in Kings. The word "humble himself" ties Amon's story to Manasseh's (verses 12, 19). The father sinned and turned back; the son sinned and did not.

decisions.choice: but he, Amon: the contrast is stressed
decisions.reason: After a negative, the conjunction means "but rather". The pronoun and name together set Amon over against his father.

decisions.choice: increased guilt: piled up guilt before Yahweh
decisions.reason: The word for guilt is one Chronicles uses for wrongdoing that brings Yahweh's anger on the people (24:18; 28:10, 13; 1 Chronicles 21:3). Amon added to it, and his death follows.

decisions.choice: added more and more to his guilt (Balanced); kept adding to his guilt (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "increased guilt" as ongoing and say "his" guilt, which is implied.

source.text: וַיִּקְשְׁר֤וּ עָלָיו֙ עֲבָדָ֔יו וַיְמִיתֻ֖הוּ בְּבֵיתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And conspired against him his servants, and they killed him in his house.

en.L: And his servants conspired against him, and they killed him in his house.
en.B: His officials plotted against him and killed him in his palace.
en.R: Some of his officials made a plot against him, and they killed him in his palace.

decisions.choice: parallel to 2 Kings 21:23
decisions.reason: The words are those of 2 Kings 21:23, except that Kings has "the servants of Amon" and "killed the king" where Chronicles has "his servants" and "killed him".

decisions.choice: his servants: his court officials
decisions.reason: "Servants" of a king are the officials of his court, as in 24:25, where Joash too was killed by his own officials. The text does not say why they acted.

decisions.choice: servants (Literal); officials (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As set for "the king's servants" in these books, and as in 2 Kings 21:23. Balanced and Readable say "palace" for the king's "house".

source.text: וַיַּכּוּ֙ עַם־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַקֹּֽשְׁרִ֖ים עַל־הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אָמ֑וֹן וַיַּמְלִ֧יכוּ עַם־הָאָ֛רֶץ אֶת־יֹאשִׁיָּ֥הוּ בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And struck [the] people of the land all the [ones] conspiring against the king Amon, and made king [the] people of the land Josiah his son in his place.

en.L: And the people of the land struck down all those who had conspired against King Amon, and the people of the land made Josiah his son king in his place.
en.B: Then the people of the land killed all who had plotted against King Amon, and the people of the land made his son Josiah king in his place.
en.R: Then the people of the land killed everyone who had plotted against King Amon. They made Amon's son Josiah king in his place.

decisions.choice: the same words as 2 Kings 21:24
decisions.reason: The verse is the same as 2 Kings 21:24 and is worded as there. Chronicles has no parallel to Kings' closing notes on Amon's reign and burial (21:25-26); Josiah's reign begins at once in chapter 34.

decisions.choice: the people of the land: the citizens of Judah as a body
decisions.reason: As in 23:13-21, the phrase means the free people of Judah, the landholders of the country, as distinct from the court in the palace. They act to keep David's line on the throne.

decisions.choice: Josiah his son: the king who will renew the covenant
decisions.reason: Josiah's reign, told in chapters 34-35, brings the greatest reform since Hezekiah's.

decisions.choice: the people of the land (every level)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 21:24, the phrase is kept at every level, since it names a group with a role of its own in Judah (m2). Readable says "They" the second time.
